newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-POPULAR FORMER CADDIE SQUEEKY MEDLEN DIES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-POPULAR FORMER CADDIE SQUEEKY MEDLEN DIES.

text.p: Jeff "Squeeky" Medlen, the longtime friend and former caddie of PGA Tour star Nick Price, died Monday night after a long battle with leukaemia at the age of 43.

Medlen, who had been Price's caddie for six years, was diagnosed with chronic myelogenous leukaemia last summer and had been undergoing treatment at a Cleveland hospital. In recent months, he underwent two bone marrow transplants.

"Squeek was more than a friend to me, he was part of my family," said Price, who dedicated his April victory at the MCI Classic to Medlen. "He was a huge part of my success, and I will always be grateful for his loyalty and devotion."

Medlen, nicknamed "Squeeky" because of his high-pitched voice, served as Price's caddy for 13 of his 14 PGA Tour victories, including triumphs at the PGA Championship in 1992 and 1994 and the British Open in 1994.
"I will forever cherish the time, the triumphs and the laughs we shared," added Price.
"Golf has lost one of its most colourful characters. His personality and sense of humour made him many friends around the world. We are all going to miss him dearly."
Medlen also caddied for John Daly when he won the 1991 PGA Championship.

"Squeeky was a young man who was loved and respected by everyone in golf, particularly the players," said PGA Tour commissioner Tim Finchem. "He put up a tremendously courageous fight. This is a tragic situation and he will be missed by all of us.
"But he will also be remembered in a very positive way because of the kind of individual he was," Finchem said.
Players, caddies and fans wore green ribbons at PGA events in recent months in support of Medlen.
